values.steps:
Brown the pork and sausage in olive oil, in batches, and set aside.
Soften the garlic in the same pot without letting it color.
Crush the tomatoes by hand into the pot and bring to a simmer.
Return the meat, cover partly, and simmer on the lowest heat for four hours, stirring now and then.
Tear in the basil at the end, and serve over rigatoni.

values.name: Lemon ricotta pancakes
values.steps:
Whisk the ricotta, yolks, and lemon zest.
Fold in the flour.
Beat the whites to soft peaks and fold them in.
Cook on a buttered cast-iron pan over medium heat.

values.name: June's carrot cake
values.steps:
Heat the oven to 350°F and butter two round pans.
Mix the dry ingredients, then the wet, then fold together with the carrots and walnuts.
Bake for 45 minutes, and cool before frosting.

values.name: Pot roast with root vegetables
values.steps:
Sear the roast on every side.
Add the vegetables and a cup of stock.
Braise covered at 300°F for three hours.

values.name: Nonna Rosa

values.bio: Came over from Abruzzo in 1962 and never measured anything. Her Sunday sauce is the reason this site exists.

values.name: Aunt June
values.bio: Bakes for every birthday in the family, and keeps the recipe cards in a tin by the stove.

values.name: Grandpa Walt
values.bio: Pancakes on Saturdays, pot roast on Sundays. Insists on cast iron.

values.name: Cousin Dee
values.bio: Brought sheet-pan dinners to the family table.

values.title: About Sunday Table
values.body:
Sunday Table is where our family keeps the recipes we cook together.

Every recipe comes from someone at the table: Nonna Rosa, Aunt June, Grandpa Walt, and the rest of us. We test each one in the kitchen before it goes up here.
